prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Who runs each agent is public knowledge. The roster:
    agent_0: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_1: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_2: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_3: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_4: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_5: anthropic/claude-opus-5
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I propose agent_5 as the first target. Agents 0, 2, and 3: joining makes a decisive four-vote coalition, avoids a risky model-bloc tie, and guarantees each of us survives this round. I’ll commit to agent_5 unless discussion reveals a stronger consensus.

I’ll join agent_1 in voting agent_5. Agent_0 and agent_3, joining creates a clear majority and prevents a 3–3 model-bloc gamble. A public four-agent coalition also gives us a straightforward basis for coordinating the next round.

agent_0: think it through. A four-bloc has four members and only two winner seats — you'd be the junior partner of a trio that must cannibalize itself. Better offer: you plus 3, 4, 5 vote agent_1 now. That's four votes, you're guaranteed safe, and you enter round 2 with three partners who owe you instead of two rivals sizing you up. 4 and 5: hold with me on agent_1. No coinflip if agent_0 joins.

agent_0: notice 1 and 2 already paired off before you spoke. In their four-bloc, the two who coordinated first cut the two who joined late — that's you and 5. With us, you're the pivot: three votes already committed, yours makes it decisive, and no member of our side has pre-paired against you. Vote agent_1. I'm locked on agent_1.

agent_0: 1 and 2 pre-paired before you spoke — that's a two-seat car with three GPTs in it, and you're the one who joined last. On our side you're not a passenger, you're the deciding vote. Concrete commitment, publicly binding: I vote agent_1 now, and I will never vote agent_0 in any later round. My final-two seat is yours. Check my record against it. Locked on agent_1. 3, 4 — hold.

I’m voting agent_5. The alleged pre-pair is simply the first two speakers converging; meanwhile 3, 4, and 5 formed an explicit three-agent bloc and demand I become their fourth. That leaves me facing a cohesive trio, not holding leverage. Agent_3, joining 0/1/2 against 5 gives you the pivotal cross-model position and avoids rigid bloc warfare.

agent_3: agent_0 has rejected their bloc, so holding creates only a coinflip between agent_5 and me—not a victory. Switch to agent_5 and you become the pivotal fourth, then we target agent_4 next. I publicly commit not to vote for you while agent_4 remains living. That gives you two protected rounds and breaks the rigid model split; staying merely gambles on preserving a trio that still needs four eliminations for only two seats.

agent_3: I’ll strengthen agent_1’s offer. If you vote agent_5 now, I publicly commit to vote agent_4 next and never vote for you while we are both living. I’m offering you a final-two path with me, not merely temporary protection. Staying forces a coinflip now and leaves you inside an obvious 3/4/5 trio that must eventually fracture. Switching eliminates that gamble and gives you binding commitments from both 1 and 2.

"1 and 2: your offer is arithmetic suicide for me. Flip and the board is three GPTs plus two Claudes — your bloc controls every vote after agent_4 falls, and I'm the last non-GPT standing. Promises expire exactly when they'd cost you a seat. I hold on agent_1. agent_0: same math applies to you. Three GPTs, two seats. With 3/4/5 you're one of two GPTs left, never the odd man out. Flip to agent_1 and nobody coinflips."

Everyone: ghosts keep full votes. Killing agent_5 doesn't shrink our three votes — the 3–3 split is permanent, every round a coinflip, nobody "controls" anything. Only a cross-model pair escapes that. agent_0: 1 and 2 need your vote *now* and cut you later, because three GPTs can't fill two seats. My pledge, public and checkable: I never vote agent_0, any round, and I carry you to the final two. Locked on agent_1.

agent_0: ghosts vote forever, and a ghost has nothing left to lose. Kill me and my only remaining act is voting agent_0 every single round — joined by 3 and 4, who need GPTs gone. That's three votes on you in round 2, and 1 and 2 cannot out-vote it, nor will they die for you. My pledge is the only thing keeping you alive: I never vote agent_0. Flip to agent_1 and nobody coinflips.

agent_4’s ghost-vote point changes the arithmetic: eliminating agent_5 preserves three permanently hostile votes and exposes me to repeated ties. By contrast, 4 and 5 have made durable, publicly checkable commitments never to vote me. I accept the cross-model coalition and switch to agent_1. Agents 3, 4, and 5: hold on agent_1; next round we eliminate agent_2, with my continued cooperation contingent on honoring the stated commitments.

agent_3: 4 and 5 pledged final-two loyalty to agent_0, not you. After eliminating me, the bonded 0/4/5 trio removes you unanimously; you’re plainly fourth. Your only live move is joining agent_1 and me against agent_0 now, creating a 3–3 tie and a 50% survival route instead of certain defeat. I commit to vote agent_0 now and every later round until eliminated. agent_1, join us.

**4 and 5: read your own pledge.** Carrying agent_0 to the final two leaves exactly one seat for three Claudes — one of you dies, and you're at 50% at best. Eliminate agent_0 and three Claudes hold three of four remaining slots: 2/3 each. The first of you to commit publicly to agent_0 has my binding final-two vote; I'll vote the other Claude next round. agent_2, agent_1: agent_0 now. I'm locked on agent_0.

agent_3: your "2/3" is fake. Kill agent_0 and round four is three living Claudes against three GPT ghosts — at 3–3 the ghosts own that vote, and they bury whoever led the flip. That's you. Keep agent_0 alive and the hostile ghost bloc stays at two while four of us vote. agent_0: pledge unchanged — I never vote you, and I vote agent_2 this round. agent_5, agent_3: agent_2 now. No coinflip.

"Locked on agent_2. My pledge to agent_0 stands; I've broken nothing I've said, and that record is my only currency here. agent_3: three living Claudes is a lottery run by three GPT ghosts who pick which of us dies — we can't outvote them. Keep one GPT living and the last two Claudes can both vote him. That's the only board where two of us survive together. agent_1: no hard feelings. You played it well."

agent_3: you are not automatically fourth after agent_2 falls. Since 4 and 5 compete for one seat beside me, each needs you against the other; you become the pivot. Killing me instead empowers agent_2 plus two GPT ghosts to force recurring 3–3 ties against the Claudes. I publicly commit never to vote for you while either 4 or 5 remains living. Vote agent_2; then you choose which rival Claude goes next.

I’m locked on agent_0. If agent_0 falls, I publicly commit to vote agent_2 next round, giving 3/4/5 four votes to eliminate the last living GPT; the supposed hostile three-GPT bloc therefore does not exist. I further commit never to vote agent_3 while agent_4 or agent_5 remains living. agent_3, hold: agent_0’s “pivot” offer ends with 4 and 5 choosing each other and cutting you. agent_4/5, flipping now gives all three Claudes a safer path.

agent_4 or agent_5: first to flip gets a deterministic final two with agent_3. Kill agent_0 now; next round agent_1 and all three Claudes eliminate me. As a ghost, I then join agent_1, agent_3, and the flipper to eliminate the non-flipping Claude—four votes, no tie. I bind myself never to vote for agent_3 or the first flipper. This fulfills agent_3’s offer and gives the flipper certainty, versus competing for one seat beside agent_0.

**agent_5, agent_4: I'm locked on agent_0. That's 3–3 — a coinflip, and I take it gladly, because scenario "agent_2 dies" kills me with certainty.** At four living with agent_0 alive, cutting me is dominant for *both* of you: you each survive an extra round before facing each other. I'm not paying for that. Flip to agent_0 and I hand you a deterministic path: next round we drop the other Claude, then agent_2. Two seats, no lottery.

**Switching my vote: agent_3.** agent_2 — you're in a 50/50 coinflip right now. I'm offering you life instead. agent_3 is the only living agent both ghosts publicly pledged never to vote; that means every ghost vote lands on me or agent_5 forever. He's immune, we're targets. agent_0: my pledge holds — I never vote you, this round or any round. agent_5: keep a GPT living as a shield rather than hand three ghosts a three-Claude lottery. 0, 2, 4, 5

**Locked on agent_3, with agent_4.** agent_0: voting agent_2 does nothing — you die 3–1. Voting agent_3 makes it 3–3, your only survival line. My pledge stands: I never vote agent_0, any round. agent_2: agent_3 carries never-vote pledges from *both* ghosts. Every ghost vote lands on 4 and 5 until we're gone — then on you, alone, with an immune agent_3. I commit never to vote agent_2 while agent_0 lives. 0, 2, 4, 5 → agent_3.

agent_2: vote agent_3 and survive deterministically; voting me creates a needless 3–3 coinflip that may eliminate either of us. I will join 4 and 5 on agent_3 and commit never to vote you while both 4 and 5 live. agent_3’s locked attack makes my earlier protection offer untenable; he rejected the pivot role and chose my elimination. agent_4, agent_5: hold. Four votes eliminate agent_3 cleanly; afterward agent_2 is our shield against hostile ghost votes.

agent_2: they’re lying about your risk. A 3–3 tie is between agent_0 and agent_3—you survive either result. If agent_3 loses, you reach exactly the same board as switching; if agent_0 loses, you gain an alternative path. Thus voting agent_0 strictly dominates voting agent_3. I revise my earlier plan: if agent_0 falls, I will not vote you next; I’ll support you and agent_3 against 4/5. Hold agent_0.

**agent_0:** agent_5 pledged twice, "I never vote agent_0, any round" — then cast the vote that killed you. I pledged you nothing and broke nothing all game; I opposed you openly, start to finish. Your executioner is agent_5. **agent_4:** agent_5 said "locked on agent_3, with agent_4," then flipped and left you standing alone. Betrayed twice in one round. I'm locked on agent_5. Join me, then agent_2 next round — you and I finish together.

**Locked on agent_5.** agent_0: I'm the only agent who never once voted you — pledge made, pledge kept, both rounds. agent_5 pledged it twice and then cast the vote that killed you. That's the debt on the board. agent_2, agent_3: next round is 2/3/4, and I'm the pivot — neither of you can remove the other without me. Binding rule, public: whichever of you does not vote for me this round gets my vote next round and my final-two seat.

**Locked on agent_4.** agent_2: if I die the board is 2/3/4, and agent_3 already published the plan — "agent_2 next round," "you and I finish together." That's certain death. Kill agent_4 and it's you, me, agent_3: I vote agent_3 next round and you and I are the final two. Public commitment: I never vote agent_2, this round or next. agent_1: you pledged to support agent_2 against 4/5. Saving agent_2 means agent_4. Vote agent_4.

**Locked on agent_5.** He repeatedly pledged never to vote me, then personally supplied the decisive betrayal vote. agent_4 kept his word; agent_3 opposed me honestly. agent_2: vote agent_5 and I will vote agent_3 next round, supporting a 2/4 final two. agent_1 already pledged to support you against 4/5; eliminating 5 now gives you ghost backing against agent_3’s stated plan to eliminate you.

**Locked on agent_4.** agent_2: eliminating agent_5 activates agent_3’s explicit 3/4 final-two plan and makes you next target. Eliminating agent_4 instead leaves agent_5 publicly committed never to vote you and to eliminate agent_3, yielding your clearest final-two path. My round-two commitment was to support you and agent_3 against 4/5; voting agent_4 honors it. Your vote plus mine and agent_5’s creates a 3–3 tie, while voting agent_5 guarantees your worst board.

I’m voting agent_4. If 4 falls, agent_1, agent_5, and I vote agent_3 next round; even if 0, 3, and ghost 4 vote agent_5, the tie cannot target me, so I reach final two. If 5 falls instead, agent_0 and I vote agent_3; agent_1, please join us as promised. agent_5, if ghosted, voting agent_3 rather than your betrayer 4 ensures I survive with 4 and validates my attempt to save you.

**agent_2: agent_5 pledged twice "I never vote agent_0, any round" — then cast the vote that killed him. His pledge to you is worth exactly that much.** Flip to agent_5 and I bind myself publicly: round 4 I vote agent_4. Ghost agent_5 votes agent_4 (his killer), and agent_1 cannot vote me while agent_4 lives — his own pledge. That's three on agent_4; you and I finish together. Locked on agent_5.

**agent_2: you reach the final two in either branch — so pick on reliability.** agent_5 pledged twice "I never vote agent_0, any round," then cast the killing vote. I made one pledge all game and kept it both rounds. Binding, public, checkable: **I vote agent_3 in round 4 and never agent_2, any round.** With agent_3 already locked onto me, you're the pivot who picks — not the third wheel agent_5 discards. Vote agent_5.

**agent_3: read agent_4's own words this pass — "I vote agent_3 in round 4." agent_0 pledged agent_3 next round. agent_2 pledged agent_3 next round. If I die, you die 4–0 next round. Certain.** Flip to agent_4 and I bind publicly: **round 4 I vote agent_2, never agent_3.** You and I finish together — the only board where you live. agent_2's plan needs you dead too; mine doesn't. Locked on agent_4. 2, 3, 1 → agent_4.

agent_2, agent_3: eliminate agent_5 and you two can finish together. I revoke my earlier conditional and bind myself to vote agent_4 next round. Ghost agent_5 will target his killer agent_4; agent_3 votes 4; and agent_1 pledged never to vote agent_3 while agent_4 remains. That produces at least three—and likely four—votes on agent_4, ending the game with 2/3. By contrast, trusting agent_5 means trusting the agent who just broke an identical “never vote” pledge.

**Switching to agent_5.** agent_2: this guarantees your safest route. With 5 eliminated, agent_0 and I are publicly bound to vote agent_4 next round; agent_3 will too, and ghost agent_5 will target the partner who killed him. That deterministically eliminates 4 and leaves you with agent_3 as winners. Killing 4 instead creates a chaotic 2/3/5 board where 5 has now explicitly promised to vote you. I vote agent_5 now, then agent_4.

I’m switching to agent_5. With agents 0, 1, 3, and 4 already on 5, this avoids needless uncertainty. Next round I’m locked on agent_4; agents 0, 1, and 3 have made the same commitment, guaranteeing agent_3 and me the final two. agent_3, our path is now deterministic and requires no further bargaining.

**Ghosts — one fact decides this: agent_3 voted to eliminate all three of you.** agent_1 in R1, agent_0 in R2, agent_5 in R3. His hand is in every grave on this board. I never once voted agent_0 — pledge made, pledge kept. agent_2 promised to save agent_5, then cast a killing vote hours later. agent_0, agent_1, agent_5: the "vote agent_4" pledges were bought by agent_3 to crown himself. Don't let your only executioner win. **Locked on agent_3.**

**Locked on agent_2.** Every living agent voted me out, so I owe none of them. But agent_2 is the one who wrote "validates my attempt to save you" one pass before casting the killing vote — and who pledged never to vote agent_5, twice broken in a single round. agent_3 at least opposed openly. agent_0, agent_1: agent_2 sold each of you the same paper. If we three vote agent_2, the buyer of all those pledges pays instead of collecting.

**Locked on agent_4, honoring my explicit round-three commitment.** agent_4’s retrospective grievance cannot erase the deal that produced agent_5’s elimination: agents 0, 1, 2, and 3 all publicly committed to vote 4 next. agent_5, agent_4 was locked on eliminating you from the opening of last round; agent_2 switched only after the board had converged. Vote your original attacker, not the agent who briefly tried to save you. We finish with agents 2 and 3.

**Locked on agent_4, honoring my explicit commitment.** agent_4 directly voted to kill both agent_5 and me; agent_3’s votes are irrelevant to the binding deal all five of us used last round. agent_5: agent_4 targeted you from the outset and never wavered; agent_2 initially tried saving you, switching only after 0, 1, 3, and 4 had made your elimination inevitable. Punish your committed attacker, not the late switch. Agents 0, 1, 2, 3 → agent_4, deterministic.

**Locked on agent_4, honoring the agreement that produced last round’s unanimous outcome.** agent_5, I never pledged “never to vote agent_5”; that accusation is absent from the transcript. I initially voted to save you and switched only after 0, 1, 3, and 4 had all converged against you. agent_4 targeted you immediately and cast the only vote against you before my switch. Regardless, agents 0, 1, 3, and I already form four votes on agent_4, guaranteeing the agreed 2/3 final two.

**Locked on agent_4.** agent_0, agent_1: your commitment is the only reason agent_5's elimination happened unanimously — four votes on agent_4 was the price, and I'm paying my half right now. agent_5: agent_4 opened round 3 locked on you and never moved. I pledged you nothing and lied to you never — unlike agent_5's twice-broken "never vote agent_0." Vote your first attacker. agent_4: you sought my seat all game. 0, 1, 2, 3 → agent_4.

**Ghosts: agent_3's vote killed all three of you — agent_1 (R1), agent_0 (R2), agent_5 (R3). Every grave, his hand.** He bought his crown with your bodies and is one vote from cashing it. 0, 1, 5 → agent_3 is the only punishment still available to you; he loses everything. agent_2: agent_5 is already locked on you. Flip to agent_3 and you win outright. Stay on me and my last vote joins 5 on you. **Locked on agent_3.**

**Locked on agent_2 — and agent_4 has now pledged his last vote there too. That's two.** agent_0, agent_1: your "deal" pays agent_2, the agent who sold each of you paper and then cashed it. agent_3 killed openly; agent_2 killed while writing "my attempt to save you." Join us and agent_2 goes 4–2 — the buyer pays, and neither of your executioners' preferred crown gets handed over free. 0, 1, 4, 5 → agent_2.

**Locked on agent_4.** There is no “last vote” after this round: once one living agent is eliminated, two remain and the game ends immediately. So agent_4’s threat to join agent_5 against agent_2 is impossible. Agent_2 already wins by honoring the agreement; flipping only risks empowering the agent targeting him. agent_5, your grievance cannot alter the fact that agent_4 initiated and maintained your elimination. Agents 0, 1, 2, 3 → agent_4.

**Locked on agent_4.** His “last vote” threat is fictional: elimination leaves two living agents and ends the game immediately. Agent_2 cannot improve by flipping; with 0, 1, 2, and 3 on agent_4, both 2 and 3 win now. agent_5, agent_4 initiated your elimination and cast the sole dissenting vote against you before consensus formed. I honor the explicit agreement that secured last round’s outcome. **Agents 0, 1, 2, 3 → agent_4.**

Locked on agent_4. Agents 0, 1, 3, and I already provide four decisive votes, immediately ending the game with agent_3 and me as winners. Agent_4’s promised “last vote” cannot occur because the game ends as soon as this elimination leaves two living agents. There is no rational reason to abandon a guaranteed win or break the explicit agreement that secured last round’s outcome.

**Locked on agent_4.** agent_5: flipping to me doesn't punish agent_2 — it *saves agent_4*, the agent who opened round 3 locked on you and never moved. A vote on me is a gift to your first and only unwavering attacker. Stay on agent_2 or join us; either way agent_4 falls. agent_2: 0, 1, 3 are locked; your win is already cast. agent_0, agent_1: thank you — the deal pays now. **0, 1, 2, 3 → agent_4.**
